chunks: Narrated to us my father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hanifa ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, may God be pleased with them, who said: Narrated to us Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Aqbah, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Bakr and Umar came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) when Fatimah (peace be upon her) was buried. In a long narration, he said to them: As for what you mentioned that I did not call you in for the task of the ritual washing of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), indeed he said: 'No one other than you shall see my private parts, except his sight will be lost.' Therefore, I did not permit you to do so. And as for my bowing over him (placing my ear near his mouth), indeed he taught me one thousand letters, each letter opening up one thousand letters. Therefore, I did not reveal it to you, as if it were the secret of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.أَمْرُ: task/job (specifically ritual washing of the dead)
key_terms.إِكْبَابِي: my bowing/placing close (specifically placing ear to mouth)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali not include Abu Bakr and Umar in washing the Prophet's body according to the narration of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the reasons behind Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) seclusion during the Prophet’s burial, citing two key factors: the prohibition of others witnessing the Prophet’s private parts to preserve their sight, and the transmission of a divine secret comprising one thousand letters. This 'secret' (Sirr) is interpreted by Shia scholars as either the 1,000 words of divine address to Moses or the 1,000 gates of esoteric knowledge (Ilm al-Batin) entrusted to the Ahl al-Bayt, distinguishing their spiritual authority from the Caliphs. The narrative underscores the unique epistemological status of Imam Ali as the sole recipient of the Prophet’s innermost teachings.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-30 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father, Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad al-Walid and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khat’tab, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali Fazzal, on the authority of Ali ibn Aqabah, on the authorityof Al-Harith ibn al-Muqayrih that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “When the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) buried Fatimah (MGB), Abu Bakr and Umar went to see him.

During a long speech he (MGB) told them, “Considering your complaint concerning why I did not call you in for the task of the ritual ablutions of the dead (ghusl) for the Prophet (MGB), I should tell you that the Prophet (MGB) had told me that except for me whoever sees the Prophets (MGB) private parts would become blind. That is why I did not inform you. However, the reason I put my head near his ear was because the Prophet (MGB) taught me one-thousand letters each of which would explain one-thousand other letters. Since this was a Prophetic secret, I did not want you to become informed about it.”
